title: Take the first n items manually
description: Write a function `take(iterable, n)` that returns a list of the first `n` items produced by `iterable`. Implement it using the manual iterator protocol: call `iter()` to get an iterator and `next()` in a loop to pull items one at a time, stopping early (without error) if `iterable` has fewer than `n` items. Do not use slicing to solve this.
hints: Any iterable (a list, a string, a generator, ...) can be turned into an iterator that hands you one item at a time on demand.
`iter(iterable)` gives you an iterator, and calling `next(iterator)` repeatedly gives you successive items until it raises `StopIteration`.

Get `it = iter(iterable)`, then loop up to `n` times calling `next(it)` inside a `try` block, appending each result to a list, and use `except StopIteration: break` to stop early if the iterable runs out before you reach `n` items.
expected_behavior: Returns a list containing up to the first n items yielded by the iterable, using iter()/next() rather than slicing; if the iterable has fewer than n items, returns all of them.
explanation: `iter(iterable)` produces an iterator object that tracks its own position. Calling `next(it)` up to `n` times pulls successive items one at a time; when the iterable is exhausted, `next` raises `StopIteration`, which is caught to stop the loop early instead of propagating an error, so `take` gracefully handles iterables shorter than `n`.
